3beta-methylserratan-21-ol and several synthetic serratane analogues showed excellent anti-tumor promotion activity, and that the presence of an alpha-methyl group at C-3, a beta-hydroxyl group at C-21, and a 14,15-double bond are important factors for the anti-tumor promotion of serratane triterpenoids.

1 and 3beta-methylserratan-21alpha-ol (13) and 3beta-hydroxyserratan-14-en-20-one (14) exhibited excellent inhibitory effects on the in vivo carcinogenicity test, and the anti-tumor promoting activities of 1 and these two synthetic compounds were stronger than that of the positive controls, oleanolic acid and caffeic acid phenethyl ester.

the triterpenoids 1, 3, 4, 5 and 13-27 are potent inhibitors of tumor promotion, and that 1, 5, 13 and 20 have strong anti-tumor promoting activities in the in vivo two- stage mouse skin carcinogenesis model induced by DMBA and TPA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a series of serratane-type compounds, and we have found a potent cancer chemopreventative agent 1, which is a natural product and easily obtainable from the two Picea species.

the isolation and identification of the triterpenoid compounds from the Picea plants and the evaluation of their anti-tumor promoting activities, especially the chemopreventative activity of 1 on mouse skin carcinogenesis, which will provide a new approach to cancer therapy.
the potential of serratane-type compounds to inhibit the tumor promotion induced by TPA and the structure-activity relationships of the serratane analogues are discussed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anti-tumor promoting activities of the compounds examined were strongly correlated with the presence of a 3alpha-methyl group, a 3beta-hydroxyl group and a 14beta-hydroxymethylene group.

the anti-tumor promoting activities of the serratane-type compounds are closely associated with their inhibitory activity on the EBV-EA activation induced by TPA, and compounds 1, 14 and 18 have a strong potential as anti-tumor promoters in the two-stage carcinogenesis test.

the presence of 3beta-hydroxy and 14alpha,15alpha-double bonds in the serratane skeleton is necessary for potent inhibition of tumor promotion, and the presence of the 21beta-hydroxy group is also important for the activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3beta-mono-O-methylated serrat-14-ene-3,21-diol derivatives are potent inhibitors of tumor promotion in both EBV-EA assay and two-stage carcinogenesis assay.

the anti-tumor promoting effect is strongly dependent on the presence of a hydroxymethyl group at C-21beta, and the presence of a double bond at C-14 and the absence of an oxygen atom at C-3beta are important for the anti-tumor promotion.
the anti-tumor promoting effect of 3beta-OMe serratane-type compounds is closely related to the structure of their side chains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3alpha,14alpha-dihydroxy group is important for the anti-tumor promoting activities of the serratane-type compounds, and the 3beta,14alpha-diol group is less effective.
the 3beta-methyl group of the serratane skeleton is important for the anti-tumor promoting effect.

3beta-methylserratanes, 3alpha-methylserratanes and their 13alpha, 14alpha-epoxides have a potential to be used as chemopreventative agents against cancer, particularly for skin cancer, because the compounds showed the potent anti-tumor promoting effects in vitro and in vivo.
